payload.blocks: The shape of the whole gateway-cluster design (ds-64l3h22msc) and its first slice. Restoring today's gateway and measuring the delay do not wait on it.
payload.headline: Gateway cluster: what may a coordination event carry ahead of git - a doorbell, the event itself, or a live coordinator?

parts.cause: Checked docs/platform/event-store/spec.md: sections 12 and 14 say there is no online coordinator (owner decision 2026-10-17) and sync is opportunistic on a timer. docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md: remote mail is recorded as an event and arrives only after that sync. An empty fetch measured 0.64 s (config note 2026-11-06), so the delay is the timer, not git.

options.cost: Small: a peer link, one message type, a hook on seal/sync. About 400-800 lines Rust across gateway and event-store wiring.
options.does: On every seal/push a gateway tells its peers which machine ref moved; peers fetch at once. Content still travels only through git.
options.gain: Delay drops from 60-300 s to about one fetch (~1 s). One truth, no new conflict rules, every law (L1, L3, no online coordinator) kept. If the gateway is down, the timer still works.
options.harm: Still pays one git push+fetch per hop; a hop needs the git remote reachable.
options.label: A. Doorbell: gateway says 'ref moved, fetch now'

options.cost: Medium-large: provisional view per consumer (mailbox, work, plan claim) plus reconcile rules.
options.does: The gateway sends the event body itself; the receiver acts on it as provisional and folds it for real when git brings it.
options.gain: Sub-second; works even when the git remote is slow.
options.harm: A second, provisional view to reconcile; every consumer must handle 'seen live but never confirmed'.
options.label: B. Event travels live, git confirms later

options.cost: Large; a superseding decision plus a consensus component.
options.does: A cluster leader grants leases/claims (who takes which plan) in real time.
options.gain: No overlap by construction; fastest decisions.
options.harm: Reverses the 2026-10-17 decision; a leader that is down stops coordination; needs consensus.
options.label: C. Gateway becomes an online coordinator

parts.recommendation: A first. It removes the measured cause (the timer) and changes no truth rule; B can be added later per consumer where A's one-fetch delay is still too slow, C only with a superseding decision.

scope.allows: Shaping the first slice as a doorbell over a gateway peer link, with git staying the only carrier of content.
scope.forbids: Changing the event store's truth or conflict rules, any code change, and ruling out B later.

parts.what: You want coordination (mail, events, plan/task placement) to move between machines fast, over a cluster of gateways, with the plan file staying the truth. Today every cross-machine event rides git: a machine seals its events into refs/fgos/events/<machine-id>, pushes, and others see it only after their own fetch timer (eventStore.sync.intervalSec, 60 s here, 300 s default).
